components.note: the ledger figure is start+complete for one cell under the advisory flock; the write figure is common.results.write_json_atomic, i.e. json encode + fsync + sha256

end_to_end.how: a real `run --fixture` of this package through common.cli, on a copy of the fixture run root with cells/ and the ledger removed; harness = wall - interpreter start-up - the summed per-cell wall_s the run recorded (which is the kernel plus the fit instrumentation)
end_to_end.includes_once_per_run_costs: the matrix write, protocol snapshot, code provenance and the interrupted sweep happen once per run and are amortised over 419 fixture cells here, so this per-cell figure OVERSTATES the production one

harness.how: end-to-end harness seconds per cell measured on the fixture, with the scale-dependent components (ledger length, result-file bytes) swapped from the fixture scale to the production scale: 0.0034545 - 0.0013335 + 0.0013218 = 0.0034428
harness.per_worker_note: the interpreter start-up and package import above is paid once per worker PROCESS, not once per cell; a scheduler that starts a fresh process per cell pays it on every cell instead, which would add 0.106 s x 2499 cells = 265 CPU-s
harness.serial_note: ledger start+complete run under an advisory flock on one lock file, so they do not parallelise: this is a floor on the wall time that no worker count beats

data_cell_correlated_hi.call_path: t21s.runner.run_data_cell -> compute_predictions (eigh of the d x d population K, one solve) then fit_pca (thin SVD of the centred N x d draw, one fit)

exponent_check.note: the measured exponent is BELOW the algorithm's by 1.93: at these sizes the kernel is not yet flop-bound (Python/allocation overhead dominates), so a projection made with the fitted exponent UNDERSTATES the cost at larger sizes and one made with the theoretical exponent overstates it at these ones

data_cell_correlated_hi.notes: the correlated geometry arm; N is held at the production aspect ratio for the hi arm (gamma = d/N fixed), so the d = 256 point IS a production correlated/hi cell

memory.rss_is: VmHWM of THIS process (resident high-water mark, never decreases); meaningful per size only when measured in a fresh subprocess
memory.ru_maxrss_is: getrusage(RUSAGE_SELF).ru_maxrss, which Linux INHERITS across fork: in a process spawned by a benchmark driver it is at least the driver's own high-water mark and says nothing about this call.  Kept for the record; rss_high_water_bytes is the one to read
memory.tracemalloc_is: peak Python-allocator bytes for this call only

notes: The protocol derives its flat scale from the PCA flop count N d min(N, d). That is NOT where the time goes at the production size: compute_predictions (the d x d eigendecomposition of K plus the QR of the direction frame) is comparable to or larger than the SVD, and at the fixture size both are dwarfed by Python overhead.

Both production sizes (d = 256 with N = 128 and with N = 1024) were run directly, in BOTH geometry arms (correlated and orthogonal), so every one of the eight data families is a MEASUREMENT of its own configuration.

reduce.bound_note: reduce reads every cell file once; measured throughput 3.7 MB/s over 419 cells (2.33 MB of input) against a warm page cache, so the step is compute-bound AT THAT SIZE.  This is not a claim about the production scale; see reduction_work.at_production_scale in RESOURCE_ESTIMATE.json

requirements.pip_dry_run_note: a real `pip install` of these pins was NOT timed: this container already satisfies them and has no guaranteed network egress, so the honest figure is the check time above. On a remote host without them, budget the download of numpy+scipy wheels (~90 MB) plus install, which is link-dependent and UNKNOWN.

transfer.note: the wall time of the transfer depends on the link, which is UNKNOWN; only the size is a fact. Measured on a build of this handoff; successive builds differ by a few tens of kB (timestamps, this report and the estimate files) - two builds of the same tree measured here were 7 702 123 and 7 764 484 bytes.
